headline: Fossil in a museum drawer is a new dinosaur

sources.title: UK dinosaur fossil identified as new long-clawed predator (Natural History Museum)
Dinosaur fossil hidden in London's Natural History Museum for 100 years identified as new species (Euronews)
A forgotten fossil reveals a fearsome dinosaur with giant claws (ScienceDaily)
New dinosaur species identified from fossil stashed in drawer for a century (EarthSky)

chunks.text: For almost 100 years, a piece of dinosaur [[skull]] sat in a drawer at London's Natural History Museum. Now it has {{turned out}} to be a [[new species]]. Scientists from University College London {{teamed up}} with the museum to study it. Their report {{came out}} on October 14, 2026, in the journal Royal Society Open Science. The dinosaur was a fast, two-legged [[meat-eater]] from a family of hunters related to T. rex. Instead of biting, they attacked with big, curved [[claws]]. It is the first of this family ever found in Europe.

verbs.correct: To be published for people to read

verbs.why: The school newspaper comes out every Friday. Her new book comes out in May. Their report came out on October 14, 2026, in the journal Royal Society Open Science.

chunks.text: The fossil was found at the bottom of a [[cliff]] on the Isle of Wight, an island off England's south coast. An [[amateur]] fossil hunter collected it with more than 1,000 others. After his death, they {{ended up}} at the museum in 1924. Experts knew it was a dinosaur, but nobody could {{figure out}} which one. So it was {{put away}} in a drawer and [[overlooked]] for decades.

verbs.wrong: To keep a fossil safe from damage
verbs.why: Kids often figure out the answer before the teacher does. Good doctors figure out the problem from a few simple tests. Experts knew it was a dinosaur, but nobody could figure out which one.

verbs.correct: To store something where it belongs

verbs.why: My son puts his toys away before bed. She puts the winter coats away every April. So it was put away in a drawer and overlooked for decades.

chunks.text: Then one of these scientists and his student {{pulled the fossil out}} of [[storage]]. They scanned it with X-rays and built a computer model. Two [[features]] {{stood out}}. One was an [[oval]] hole where the [[spinal cord]] met the brain. The other was a [[crest]] shaped like an [[hourglass]]. These details {{set the dinosaur apart}} from all known species.

verbs.wrong: To make a copy of an old object
verbs.why: He pulls his keys out of his bag at the front door. She pulls an old photo out of a box. Then one of these scientists and his student pulled the fossil out of storage.
Her bright red coat stands out in a crowd. One answer always stands out as the best. Two features stood out.

verbs.why: Great service sets this small hotel apart from others. His deep voice sets him apart from other singers. These details set the dinosaur apart from all known species.

chunks.text: The dinosaur was probably about as tall as a person. It likely {{hunted down}} small dinosaurs, lizards and mammals. The scientist who led the study says it was not the top [[predator]] of its time. The find also {{backs up}} an idea that this family spread from Asia through Europe. Its scientific name means "unconquered female warrior." It honors the giant hunters the family later became. The scientists also hope the name gives [[bullied]] people the strength not to {{give up}}.

verbs.why: Owls hunt down mice at night. Lions hunt down slow or weak animals. It likely hunted down small dinosaurs, lizards and mammals.

mainIdea.s: A skull piece that sat unnoticed in a museum for a century belongs to a new kind of dinosaur. It is also the first of its group found in Europe, which supports a theory about how the group spread.
mainIdea.why: The skull piece turned out to be a new species. It is the first of its family in Europe, and it backs up an idea about its travels.

mainIdea.s: Scientists dug up a new type of dinosaur at a tall English cliff in October 2026. They say the giant animal was the top hunter of its time and larger than any other meat-eater in Europe.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the fossil was found over 100 years ago and sat in a drawer. The scientist who led the study says it was not the top predator, and it was about human size.

mainIdea.s: A London museum will close its dinosaur hall for two years to repair the roof and old cases. Visitors can still see a few famous skeletons at a smaller show in another part of the building.
mainIdea.why: This is about an old skull piece that scientists pulled out of storage. Scans showed it belonged to a new species of dinosaur.

tf.s: The skull piece turned out to belong to a new species of dinosaur.

tf.s: The fossil was found by a team of scientists in 2026.

tf.s: For decades, nobody could figure out which dinosaur the fossil belonged to.
tf.why: Experts knew it belonged to a dinosaur, but not which one, so it stayed in a drawer.

tf.s: Two features of the skull stood out when scientists scanned it.
tf.why: An oval hole and a crest shaped like an hourglass set the dinosaur apart from all known species.

tf.s: The scientist who led the study says the dinosaur was the top predator of its time.
tf.why: He says it was not the top predator. Still, it probably hunted down small dinosaurs, lizards and mammals.

tf.s: Many dinosaurs of this family had already been found in Europe.
tf.why: It is the first of its family ever found in Europe, and the find backs up an idea about how the family spread.

lines.text: Did you see the story about the dinosaur in the museum drawer?
A piece of skull sat in a drawer in London for almost 100 years. It just {{turned out}} to be a brand-new species.
A hundred years? It was [[right under their noses]] the whole time.
Exactly. Experts knew it was a dinosaur, but nobody could {{figure out}} which one.
Pretty much. Then a scientist and his student {{pulled it out}} again and scanned it.
Two features {{stood out}}, a strange hole and a crest shaped like an hourglass. That's what {{set it apart}}.
Okay, [[what a find]]. Was it a big dinosaur?
About as tall as a person, with huge curved claws. It probably {{hunted down}} small animals.
The scientist who led the study says it wasn't even the top predator of its time.
Still, I'm glad there were no people in those days. We [[dodged a bullet]].
Ha! And its name means "unconquered female warrior." The scientists want the name to give bullied people the strength not to {{give up}}.
I love that. That's [[a nice touch]].
